text: Absolutely do not recommend ever coming to this hospital. Was given ciprofloxacin + cerebrex for "prostatitis" (I saw my paperwork and saw no bacterial infection, so i was given this for no reason!!) by a urologist. The urologist was kind but I was given one of the most dangerous medicines in modern medicine. they absolutely do not follow most up to date health guidelines. I have had my health destroyed at 22 years old by this hospital and the damage will most likely be permanent.  By the 5th dose I had a nervous system damage which destroyed my breathing pattern followed by anaphylactic shock and I am still trying to recover my health 112 days later. I was not informed of the possible deadly side effects this drug could have. My neurologist believes the damage will be permanent due to its severity. I am short of breath all day and cannot take care of myself due to this hospitals mistake. I also have developed autonomic neuropathy as a result of this hospitals procedures, my life has been ruined by this hospital. Please stop dispensing fluoroquinolone drugs like they're candy, they're meant for confirmed infections and as a last line treatment!

text:
Quite a disappointing visit to this hospital. This review is in relation to the hospital's drive through covid19 testing facility.

We previously registered with the hospital's online system for drive through rtpcr testing and received no response for a whole day (either via phone or email). The next day, after calling them repeatedly, we were finally informed that the drive through rtpcr testing is available from 9 am until 2 pm, and that no booking is required.

Upon reaching the facility at 1.30 pm, we were told that we could not have the test done, as only 100 slots are available. Our various attempts to clarify the situation went in vain and the nurses / staff were rude and did not spend much time explaining further possibilities.

Lack of clarity and obligation towards the general public is something that makes this a very disappointing visit. They could at least provided some affirmation in terms of the situation rather than being completely dismissive. A truly sad experience.

restaurant_name: โรงพยาบาลบางโพ / Bangpo Hospital
text:
I happened to have to make two visits to Bang Po Hospital.  Four or five years ago, I broke my left foot.  I was staying in the Saphan Kwai district, close to Bang Po.  My foot was X-rayed, I was shown the cracked bone and the orthopedic surgeon advised me to wear a special shoe and keep my feet up for two weeks.  He and the nurses and staff were very professional and able.

Two years ago, I developed a bad infection in my right elbow.  It hardened like stone and started to spread down to my hand and up to my shoulder.  Again, I went to Bang Po Hospital.  They admitted me and the admitting doctor wan another orthopedic surgeon.  It turned out I had MRSA, myocin resistant staph infection.  Luckily, my surgeon opened my elbow and cleared out as much of the infectious material in my elbow that he could reach.  It took awhile but I was OK.  The charges for both trips were staggeringly cheap.  With MRSA, I had a private room for a week, outpatient for a week, surgery, prescription meds, etc. and it was about $2,000 US.  I cannot recommend this hospital strongly enough!

text:
A message to OPD MED: I went for a health checkup for insurance purposes. You cannot use the excuse that there are too many patients to complete the insurance paperwork for me.

1. After the checkup, I was asked to pay, but when I checked the documents, they were incomplete. The hospital stamp wasn't there, and other test results weren't properly sealed together with the envelope to send to the insurance company. I had to take them back to get them completed, wasting almost an hour. 🙃
2. They brought the documents, but then asked for additional payment, saying they forgot to key in the cost of one test item. 🙃
At first, I wouldn't have minded, saying there were too many patients, but didn't they consider the time I wasted waiting and the potential return trips to the hospital because of incomplete documents?

And then...
3. The insurance company called to inform me that the doctor had entered one item incomplete (it was in the sealed envelope that we couldn't review, but OPD MED needed to check before sealing). This caused me to waste time completing the additional documents and traveling back to the insurance company. 🙃

I reiterate, don't use the excuse of too many patients to allow for incomplete service. I paid the full amount myself.

However, I would like to commend most of the staff; they were lovely, polite, and courteous. There was only one person speaking curtly and appearing unwilling to provide service. I'm not sure if this resulted in incomplete documentation, but what's certain is that the customer wasted time. Instead of getting everything done in one go, the process was delayed. Please improve your service. 🙂
